title: PSUB Operator Guide
subtitle: A faster, safer path for Windows Python security release builds
notes: Hero slide uses the repository background asset.

title: Why PSUB
subtitle: The operator problem it solves on a Windows build machine
body: One entry point for prerequisite checks, build settings, and launch
Less guesswork when Visual Studio, SDK, or bootstrap Python drift
Clearer failure handling than raw batch files alone
callouts: Operators stay in one UI instead of jumping between scripts, docs, and environment probes.

title: Standard Operator Workflow
subtitle: The repeatable sequence that keeps failures visible
body: Open PSUB
Confirm prerequisites
Set source and bootstrap Python
Create or refresh doc-venv
Start build
Review log and collect artifacts
callouts: The same sequence now works cleanly with Visual Studio Professional 2022.

title: Prerequisites That Matter
subtitle: What must be green before you trust a build run
body: Visual Studio 2019 or 2022 with Desktop development with C++
MSVC toolchains for x64, x86, and ARM64
Windows 10 SDK 10.0.19041.0 or later
Bootstrap Python 3.10 or 3.12
Git for Windows on PATH
.NET Framework 3.5 for legacy Python 3.10 MSI flows
callouts: PSUB links missing prerequisites directly to setup guides.
Do not use Microsoft Store alias paths or Python 3.13 as bootstrap.

title: Live UI Walkthrough
subtitle: Only a few fields matter for a clean run
body: Use Auto-Detect to fill Bootstrap Python
Confirm SourcePath and doc-venv
Start Build opens a separate live terminal
callouts: Focus on the build form, not every control in the page.

title: What We Verified On A Clean Machine
subtitle: Recent improvements that reduced operator friction
body: Visual Studio Professional 2022 now works end-to-end on a new machine
Bootstrap autodetect rejects WindowsApps aliases and finds real Python installs
The Windows SDK field now prefills from autodetect instead of a stale default
Python 3.10 MSI/doc handling and artifact naming are now more robust
callouts: These were practical fixes discovered during a fresh-machine setup, not just theoretical cleanup.

title: Common Failure Cases
subtitle: Most blocked runs still fall into a short fixable list
body: Git missing from PATH
Windows SDK or MSVC toolchains incomplete
Wrong bootstrap Python version or alias path
Missing doc-venv or Sphinx dependencies
Python 3.10 WiX or .NET 3.5 dependency issue
callouts: Install Git for Windows and reopen the shell.
Use the setup guides linked by the prerequisites panel.
Switch to a real Python 3.10 or 3.12 executable.
Run Setup Virtual Environment before retrying.
Enable .NET Framework 3.5 for older 3.10 MSI flows.

title: Takeaways
subtitle: What operators should remember after the walkthrough
body: Treat PSUB as the primary operator entry point for Windows Python release builds
Trust the prerequisite panel before starting a long build
Use the UI for clarity and the CLI when you need scripted repeatability
callouts: If the machine is green and bootstrap Python is real, the rest of the workflow becomes predictable.
